newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 16.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on +44 (0)171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com
-- NATWEST MARKETS FACES REVAMP

Facing heavy criticism from institutional investors over its recent performance, National Westminster Bank is reported to be considering an overhaul of its NatWest Markets investment banking arm. NatWest Markets directors appear set to recommend to the bank's board that it be scaled down through the transfer of its corporate lending and treasury operations into the commercial bank.
-- MCI CHIEF SAYS BT KNEW OF INVESTMENT STRATEGY

Despite claims by British Telecommunications that they were seeking his dismissal after last week's surprise MCI profits warning, MCI president and chief operating officer Timothy Price stated on Tuesday he expects to be running MCI 'for a long time to come'. Price declared BT was fully aware of his company's investment strategy, as it was formulated by both BT and MCI, then presented, reviewed and approved by BT and MCI board members.
-- FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN UK LEAPS 24 PERCENT TO RECORD 9.3BN STG

According to a government report to be presented on Wednesday by trade and industry secretary Margaret Beckett, foreign direct investment in the UK rose 24 percent in 1996 to a record 9.34 billion stg. The investment was headed by a 1.7 million stg injection from South Korea's LG to construct an electronics complex in South Wales and Beckett is expected to use the report to emphasise the government's commitment to encouraging foreign investment.
-- STRONG POUND 'PUTS 100,000 JOBS AT RISK'

According to Andrew Sentance, director of the London Business school's Centre for Economic Forecasting, the recent strength of the pound could lead to British manufacturers shedding 100,000 jobs over the next year as sterling could 'knock two percent off manufacturing output growth'. In a speech to the Foundation for Manufacturing and Industry, Sentance pointed out that sterling has strengthened by more than 20 percent in the past year measured against a trade-weighted basket of other currencies.
-- INVESTORS ATTACK BA LIVERY REVAMP

At its annual meeting on Tuesday, British Airways met with friction from private shareholders angered more with the group's new 60 million stg livery than last week's cabin crew strike. Shareholders were upset with the new 'world' designs on BA aircraft fins, believing the airline was moving away from British culture, a complaint Ayling denied, though he did state elements of 'Britishness' were standing in the way of the company's development plans.
-- SALOMON GIVES BZW WARNING OVER F1 FLOAT

US investment bank Solomon Brothers, the group looking to float the Formula One Holdings motor racing group, has issued UK merchant bank BZW an ultimatum to end advertisement of a rival plan by BSkyB or leave the team altogether. Christopher Purslow, the Salomon director in charge of the FOH team insisted BZW assure it no privileged information relating to the deal would be passed on to a third party, adding if BZW reacted with hostility there was 'a queue of banks halfway down the city' interested in joining the syndicate.
-- RAISIO UP 34 PERCENT ON US LICENCE DEAL

Finnish food and chemicals group Raisio saw its shares rise 34 percent on Tuesday, following the announcement it had signed a licensing agreement with a division of US consumer healthcare products group Johnson & Johnson for its Benecol cholesterol-cutting margarine. The deal grants the J&J division exclusive rights to use the key Benecol ingredient in a product that is expected to gain a large international market.
-- KENWOOD TAKES CHARGE AND CHOPS PAYOUT

Kenwood Appliances have announced pre-tax losses of 11.4 million stg, exceptional charges of 15.4 million stg, operating profits down 50 percent to 8.8 million stg and sales up three percent for the year to April 4. The group's new management, however, remain confident that recent actions, including a workforce reduction by 365, will begin to show positive effects in the second half.
-- BANKS CALCULATE COST OF BT/MCI

Banks and investors have revealed that if the British Telecoms -MCI deal falls apart, international investment banks and hedge funds will face with multi-million pound losses stemming from deals relating to the relative values of the company's shares. Due to the secretive nature of propriety trading an exact figure on the collapse cannot be calculated, but with 10 percent of BT shares involved in arbitrage on the MCI merger, the multi-million pound figure seems acceptable.
-- SHIELD EXPECTS EARLY TEST CLEARANCE IN US

UK healthcare company Shield Diagnostics announced on Tuesday that it expects to receive US approval for its new heart disease test within the next six months. The announcement came as the group reported its yearly results to March 31, including pre-tax losses of 1.3 million stg, R&D expenditure of 1.1 million stg, turnover down from 5.83 million stg to 5.75 million stg and net cash of 1.16 million stg. Shield is already in negotiations with a number of companies to which it may licence the drug test.
